skills.name: Say why learning CRE matters and how it grows good values
skills.mastery: The child says CRE helps people know God, grow in values such as honesty, respect, love and responsibility, and live well with others. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the right answer
pick the right answer in a short story
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: Values in the Ten Commandments, the first list of values a learner meets in CRE. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
The Bible as God's word, which CRE studies. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks CRE is only for passing exams.

example.question: Why do we learn CRE?
example.correct_answer: To grow in good values and know God

misconceptions.cause: Exams are what school rewards, so every subject is seen as a mark.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only to pass exams" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Ask learners to write how one CRE lesson changed what they did that week.
misconceptions.feedback: CRE helps us know God and live with good values.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks CRE applies only in church.

example.question: Where should we show the values learnt in CRE?
example.correct_answer: At home, school and church

misconceptions.cause: CRE talks about God, and God is linked with church.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only in church" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: List places values are needed: home, school, the matatu, online. Match a value to each.
misconceptions.feedback: We show values everywhere we live.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Picks boldness in getting one's own way as a value, mixing confidence with selfishness, instead of honesty.

example.question: Which is a value learnt in CRE?
example.wrong_answer: Getting your own way at any cost
example.correct_answer: Honesty

misconceptions.cause: Some values sound alike and the learner picks a word that "sounds strong".
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Getting your own way at any cost" beside "Honesty" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Sort cards into values and vices; give each value an action that shows it.
misconceptions.feedback: Honesty is a value; cheating is not.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks CRE is only a list of rules, not also knowing God and growing in character.

example.question: What is Christian Religious Education mainly about?
example.wrong_answer: Learning rules so as to avoid punishment
example.correct_answer: Knowing God through the Bible and growing in values for responsible living

misconceptions.cause: Many lessons end with "do" and "do not", so the learner hears only rules.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Learning rules so as to avoid punishment" beside "Knowing God through the Bible and growing in values for responsible living" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask what each lesson taught about God, then what it taught about living. Both together are CRE.
misconceptions.feedback: CRE helps us know God and grow in values. It is more than rules.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

skills.name: Tell the two accounts of creation and what they teach about God
skills.mastery: The child says the first account (Genesis 1) has God creating in six days and resting on the seventh, with human beings made last in God's image, and the second (Genesis 2) has the man formed from the dust and given life by God's breath and placed in the garden of Eden; and names attributes of God (powerful, creator, good, caring, orderly). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the right answer
pick the right answer in a short story
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: Genesis 3 follows the second creation account. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
God's rest on the seventh day closes the first account. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
Attributes of God, which the creation accounts show. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Says God worked for seven days in Genesis 1, counting the day of rest as a working day.

example.question: In how many days did God create in Genesis 1, before resting?
example.correct_answer: Six days

misconceptions.cause: The week has seven days, so the learner counts the rest day as a working day.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Seven days of work" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Number Genesis 1 day by day on the board; stop at day six; write "rest" on day seven.
misconceptions.feedback: God created in six days and rested on the seventh.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Puts man formed from the dust in the first account (Genesis 1), mixing it with the second (Genesis 2:7).

example.question: In which account is man formed from the dust?
example.correct_answer: The second account in Genesis 2

misconceptions.cause: The two accounts are read as one story.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The first account in Genesis 1" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Make two columns, Genesis 1 and Genesis 2, and write where each detail comes from.
misconceptions.feedback: The man formed from the dust is in Genesis 2.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Names God as all-forgiving as an attribute shown in the creation accounts, instead of one the accounts show, such as creator and orderly.

example.question: Which attribute of God is shown in Genesis 1 by "God said... and it was so"?
example.correct_answer: God is all-powerful: he creates by his word

misconceptions.cause: The learner names any attribute of God, not one the accounts show.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "God forgives sins" beside "God is all-powerful: he creates by his word" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: For each attribute, ask for the verse in Genesis 1-2 that shows it.
misconceptions.feedback: God is powerful and the creator of all things.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks man was made first in Genesis 1, before plants and animals.

example.question: In Genesis 1, on which day were human beings made?
example.correct_answer: On the sixth day, after the plants and animals

misconceptions.cause: In Genesis 2 the man is made before the plants appear, and the orders mix.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "On the first day" beside "On the sixth day, after the plants and animals" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Write Genesis 1 in six boxes and Genesis 2 as a separate story; note the difference as one of the points to discuss.
misconceptions.feedback: In Genesis 1, people were made on the sixth day, after plants and animals.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

learning_experiences: brainstorm on how they care for animals, fish, and birds and make summary notes,
read Genesis 2:15-20, James 3: 7 and discuss the responsibilities given to human beings by God,

write sensitisation messages on charts or posters on the importance of good stewardship over animals, fish, and birds,
display the poster or chart in class or on the school notice boards,
compose a poem on how they take care of animals, fish and birds in their environment.
key_inquiry_questions: Why should you care for animals, fish, and birds?
How can you reduce conflicts between human beings and wild animals?

outcomes.text: explain the biblical responsibilities given to human beings over creation
discuss ways they can protect animals, fish, and birds

skills.name: Say what God asked people to do for animals, fish and birds, and how to protect them
skills.mastery: The child says God gave people the duty to rule over and care for animals, fish and birds (Genesis 1:26-28), and names ways to protect them (not hunting illegally, not polluting water, leaving nests, giving shelter and food). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the right answer
pick the right answer in a short story
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.
Grade 5: the work God gave people over creation. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
Choosing activities that build up rather than harm. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Reads "rule over" (Genesis 1:28) as permission to use animals in any way, even cruelly.

example.question: What does "rule over the fish, the birds and every living creature" mean?
example.wrong_answer: People may treat animals any way they like
example.correct_answer: Care for them as God's caretakers

misconceptions.cause: The word "rule" is heard as power to do anything.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "People may treat animals any way they like" beside "Care for them as God's caretakers" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 1:28 with 2:15: rule as God's caretaker who will answer to him.
misconceptions.feedback: Ruling over means caring for them as God's creation.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks killing birds with a catapult for fun is harmless because birds are many.

example.question: Boys kill birds with a catapult for fun. Is this good stewardship?
example.correct_answer: No: it harms God's creatures for no need

misconceptions.cause: The learner sees some harm as normal, such as killing birds for fun.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes, there are many birds" beside "No: it harms God's creatures for no need" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: List daily acts that harm animals and the caring choice for each.
misconceptions.feedback: Keeping rivers clean and nests safe protects them.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks creation belongs to people.

example.question: To whom does creation belong?
example.wrong_answer: To people to use as they wish
example.correct_answer: To God, who gave us the care of it

misconceptions.cause: Owning a cow or a dog feels like full ownership.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "To people to use as they wish" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Read Psalm 24:1: the earth is the Lord's. We care for what is his.
misconceptions.feedback: Creation belongs to God and we care for it.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks poaching wild animals is fine if a family is poor.

example.question: A man kills elephants for their tusks to feed his family. What does stewardship teach?
example.wrong_answer: It is fine because he is poor
example.correct_answer: It is wrong: wildlife is God's creation and protected by law

misconceptions.cause: Poverty makes any income seem justified.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It is fine because he is poor" beside "It is wrong: wildlife is God's creation and protected by law" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Discuss honest work and the Kenya Wildlife Service; God's care for creatures (Genesis 1:21-22).
misconceptions.feedback: Poaching harms God's creation and breaks the law. There are honest ways to earn.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

skills.name: Say what God asked people to do for plants and how to use them well
skills.mastery: The child says God gave plants for food and asked people to work and take care of the garden (Genesis 1:29 and 2:15), and says caring for plants (planting trees, not cutting without replacing) protects the land and can bring income. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the right answer
pick the right answer in a short story
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: Proposed: this skill builds on it. To confirm by a CRE teacher.
Caring for God's creation, met in Grade 5. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
A seed that grows into a tree: the care of plants pictured in a parable. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks cutting trees for charcoal without replanting does no harm, because there are many trees.

example.question: A family cuts trees for charcoal every month. What does stewardship ask?
example.correct_answer: Plant more trees than are cut

misconceptions.cause: Trees are everywhere and the learner does not see them running out.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Nothing: there are many trees" beside "Plant more trees than are cut" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Show the cost: a tree takes years to grow. Plan a "cut one, plant two" rule for the school.
misconceptions.feedback: Plant a new tree when we cut one.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God gave plants only for beauty, missing Genesis 1:29: plants for food.

example.question: Why did God give plants, according to Genesis 1:29?
example.wrong_answer: Only to make the earth beautiful
example.correct_answer: For food, as well as beauty

misconceptions.cause: The learner remembers only the beauty of Eden.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only to make the earth beautiful" beside "For food, as well as beauty" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 1:29 and 2:9: plants for food and beauty.
misconceptions.feedback: God gave plants for food and asked us to care for the garden.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks caring for plants is only about food and cannot earn an income.

example.question: How can responsible use of plants help the economy?
example.wrong_answer: It cannot; plants are only food
example.correct_answer: Cash crops, timber and fruit bring income and jobs

misconceptions.cause: The learner thinks farming is for food only and does not see markets.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It cannot; plants are only food" beside "Cash crops, timber and fruit bring income and jobs" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Name crops grown for sale in the area and what the money pays for.
misconceptions.feedback: Good crop care gives food and income.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks burning bushes to clear land is good stewardship because it is quick.

example.question: A farmer burns the bush to clear land every year. Is this responsible use of plants?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, it is the quickest way
example.correct_answer: No: it kills soil life and causes erosion; there are better ways

misconceptions.cause: Burning is common and seen as normal.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes, it is the quickest way" beside "No: it kills soil life and causes erosion; there are better ways" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: List effects of burning on soil and wildlife; compare with clearing and composting.
misconceptions.feedback: Burning harms the soil and creatures. Responsible stewards clear land carefully and keep soil covered.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

skills.name: Tell good use from misuse of natural resources
skills.mastery: The child names uses (water for drinking and farming, soil for crops) and misuse (polluting rivers, wasting water, cutting trees without replanting) and the effects (drought, soil erosion, hunger, disease), and says the Bible calls for careful use. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: pick the right answer
pick the right answer in a short story
find the false step in a learner's reason

prerequisites.reason: Responsible use of plants is one case of using natural resources. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
God's work for people: caring for creation. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks pouring waste into a river is fine because the water carries it away.

example.question: A factory pours waste into a river. What is this?
example.wrong_answer: Good use: the river carries it away
example.correct_answer: Misuse: it poisons water for fish and people

misconceptions.cause: Waste poured out of sight seems to disappear.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Good use: the river carries it away" beside "Misuse: it poisons water for fish and people" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Follow the waste: river, fish, people downstream who drink it.
misconceptions.feedback: Polluting the river is misuse of water.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks cutting trees has no effect on the land, missing soil erosion and drought.

example.question: Which is an effect of cutting trees without replanting?
example.correct_answer: Soil erosion and drought

misconceptions.cause: The learner has not linked trees and rain.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "More rain forever" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new situation.
misconceptions.help: Show a picture of a bare hillside after rain: gullies, mud in the river.
misconceptions.feedback: Cutting trees without replanting causes erosion and drought.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a bare, swept field is good use of soil, though it washes away in rain.

example.question: Which is good use of soil?
example.wrong_answer: Sweeping it bare so it looks tidy
example.correct_answer: Keeping it covered with crops or mulch

misconceptions.cause: Bare soil looks tidy and "clean".
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Sweeping it bare so it looks tidy" beside "Keeping it covered with crops or mulch" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Show soil cover (mulch, crops) and explain it holds the soil in rain.
misconceptions.feedback: Planting crops and covering soil uses it well.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks natural resources such as water and forests can never run out.

example.question: Can natural resources such as water and forests run out?
example.correct_answer: Yes, if they are misused; we must use them well

misconceptions.cause: The learner reasons that what God made cannot fail.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "No, God made them endless" beside "Yes, if they are misused; we must use them well" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Show a dried river or a cleared forest in Kenya; read Genesis 2:15 as a call to care.
misconceptions.feedback: Resources can run out when misused. Caring for them is our God-given work.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes, deleting removes it for ever" beside "No: others may have saved or shared it" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Show how screenshots and forwarding work; think before posting (Philippians 4:8).
misconceptions.feedback: Once posted, something can be saved and shared even after you delete it. Think before you post.
